title: Technical Note: Physical Dynamics of Unit Activity — From Jada to Jeevan

passages.heading: abstract
passages.text: Abstract

passages.heading: abstract
passages.text: The state-dynamic model of coexistence describes existence through units whose activities establish configurations, interactions, and continuing order. Quantitative development can begin by adopting established physical laws for the insentient, or jada, domain. This note proposes a bridge between Lagrangian and Hamiltonian descriptions of material dynamics and the four aspects of the active unit: form (roop), relative power (guna), essential nature (svabhav), and innateness (dharma). It also examines law (niyam), regulation (niyantran), and balance (santulan) as connected questions about definite conduct, the conditions that sustain it, and participation in a larger order. A damped, driven oscillator illustrates configuration, interaction, persistence, and dynamic balance. The approach then extends to material composition, pranic organisation, and the body associated with Jeevan. Jeevan’s constitution remains invariant, while understanding, evaluation, and dispositions require a distinct account of refinement. Saturation remains an ontological premise, and bodily association requires an explicit interface for coupled predictions. The note establishes an initial research specification: conceptual correspondences, a worked physical example, a proposed architecture, validation requirements, and unresolved questions. Mathematical formulations are collected in the appendices.

passages.heading: 1-the-question-and-intended-achievement
passages.text: 1. The question and intended achievement

passages.heading: 1-the-question-and-intended-achievement
passages.text: How can the qualitative account of unit activity become a model with explicit laws of change? The State-Dynamic Model of Coexistence already distinguishes constitution, changing conditions, mutuality, disposition, and evidence. Its occurrence relations identify what a coherent account must include. A quantitative extension must additionally specify variables, durations, interactions, and rules that determine particular changes.

passages.heading: 1-the-question-and-intended-achievement
passages.text: This note adopts established physics for material activity at the scale being studied. Jada includes material and pranic units, including the human body. The new theoretical work principally concerns the interpretation of physical descriptions within the ontology, Jeevan’s refinable state, and the interface through which sentient activity participates bodily. This commitment supplies a practical starting point; the correspondence between particular physical entities and the source’s atomic account remains a question for investigation (§9).

passages.heading: 1-the-question-and-intended-achievement
passages.text: The intended achievement is a usable specification for the next stage of the study. It should identify which descriptions can be supplied by physics, explain how they answer the four-aspect and orderliness questions, and state what additional structure is required for Jeevan. A successful next version will reproduce an independently understood material example, extend it to a bounded case of human participation, and make clear which predictions depend on measured inputs and which depend on a proposed learning or interface rule.

passages.heading: 1-the-question-and-intended-achievement
passages.text: This initial version develops the conceptual bridge and an analytical example. It supplies no fitted Jeevan dynamics or experimental validation. The main study remains the qualitative synthesis; this companion develops a possible quantitative extension.

passages.heading: 2-the-active-unit-and-its-continuing-organisation
passages.section: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation
passages.text: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation

passages.heading: 2-the-active-unit-and-its-continuing-organisation
passages.section: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation
passages.text: A unit is an active bearer with definite constitution and form. Its strength in state and power in motion are inseparable; effort, motion, and result describe connected aspects of its continuing activity. Form, property, essential nature, and dharma describe that same unit through its configuration, effective participation, characteristic conduct, and innateness (SB, pp. 58–62, 248–252, 256–257; MVD, pp. 47, 50–51).

passages.heading: 2-the-active-unit-and-its-continuing-organisation
passages.section: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation
passages.text: The bridge begins with this continuity. A physical state describes selected conditions of a unit at a considered time. An evolution law relates those conditions to further conditions through actual interactions. The time interval marks a duration within activity. It does not separate effort, motion, and result into three successive processes. The parent study’s occurrence index can therefore be related to observation times or numerical integration intervals without assuming that nature proceeds through discrete pauses.

passages.heading: 2-the-active-unit-and-its-continuing-organisation
passages.section: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation
passages.text: Constitution, configuration, and environment have different roles. A mechanical assembly can retain its parts while their positions change. A compound can form or disintegrate. A body can maintain its organisation while taking in and releasing matter. An adopted physical model must specify which of these changes it represents and when its original description ceases to apply. The distinction between a containing whole and interacting participants is especially important: a model boundary identifies a system for study, while a claim that a further unit exists requires an account of its definite organisation and conduct (MVD, p. 42; SB, p. 260).

passages.heading: 2-the-active-unit-and-its-continuing-organisation
passages.section: 2. The active unit and its continuing organisation
passages.text: Saturation grounds the intrinsic activeness of units within the coexistence account. In this extension it remains a standing ontological premise. The physical equations account for the finite energies, forces, and exchanges of the selected material system. A future physical explanation of saturation would require additional definitions and evidence (§9; parent study, Appendix A.2).

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: 3. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian descriptions

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: 3.1 Describing structure and change

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: A Lagrangian description starts with suitable coordinates, their rates of change, and a function specifying the dynamics. For a familiar mechanical system this function is kinetic energy minus potential energy. The corresponding action is accumulated over a time interval, and stationary action yields the equations of motion. The principle concerns stationarity, which need not be a minimum (Tong-L, §2.1).

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: A Hamiltonian description replaces velocities with conjugate momenta, where this change of variables is locally invertible. It presents evolution through first-order equations on the space of possible states. The two descriptions then give the same physical trajectories from corresponding initial conditions. The Hamiltonian is particularly useful for examining symmetries and conserved quantities (SICM-H, §3.1).

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: Neither formulation selects a physical model by name alone. Each application needs a specified constitution, interaction law, initial state, and surrounding conditions. Mechanical action, measured in energy multiplied by time, also has a different meaning from purposeful human action. The mathematical construction is set out in Appendix A.

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: 3.2 Exchanges and levels of description

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: Forces supplied by the surroundings and dissipative effects can be included explicitly in the Lagrange equations. A spring, moving mass, and damper provide a simple example. Its mechanical energy changes through work supplied to the assembly and energy transferred to its surroundings (MIT-D, pp. 1–4).

passages.heading: 3-lagrangian-and-hamiltonian-descriptions
passages.text: The broader jada programme will choose models appropriate to the phenomenon: mechanical motion, chemical transformation, heat and material transport, or bodily regulation. Hamiltonian and Lagrangian methods provide an entry into this programme. Atomic and molecular applications require the relevant quantum descriptions; a pranic model requires the processes that sustain bodily organisation. These applications have their own state variables and empirical parameters. A single classical particle trajectory is insufficient to specify all of them.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: The four aspects are co-present descriptions of one active bearer. Their physical representation will consequently overlap. Coordinates, interaction laws, and persistence conditions jointly help answer the four questions; there is no requirement to assign each aspect to one mathematical quantity.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: Aspect Meaning in the unit account Proposed use in a physical model Roop — form Definite configuration, dimensions, density, and boundary-framework Specify geometry, composition, spatial distributions, and the configuration that is present. Include internal conditions needed to explain how that form can change. Guna — relative power The unit’s operative influence in actual mutuality Describe responses, interactions, transfer rates, and the resulting effects on participating units. State the conditions under which a capacity is expressed. Svabhav — essential nature The functional character and usefulness of the unit’s powers within its order Identify whether the modelled participation integrates or disintegrates material organisation, or vitalises or devitalises a pranic organisation. Dharma — innateness What is borne according to order: existence in the material order, with growth included in the pranic order State the order being represented and examine the continuity of its organisation and participation. Distinguish that organisation’s persistence from the continued existence of its constituents after dissolution.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: The definitions follow the four-aspect account (MVD, pp. 42, 47, 50–51, 77, 115; SB, pp. 179–180, 248–252, 256–257). The physical representations in the final column are this note’s proposal.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: For roop, position alone can be inadequate: two bodies with the same outline can differ in temperature, composition, or internal stress and therefore evolve differently. These conditions belong in the physical state, even where their relation to outward form is indirect. For guna, an interaction term and the response it produces are more informative than an isolated material constant. Elastic stiffness, for example, contributes to a definite response only within a particular configuration and encounter.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: Svabhav gives the effect its order-specific significance. Formation and dissolution both occur within material participation. In a living organisation, the further question concerns nourishment, growth, repair, and decline. Dharma states the innateness whose manifestation is being considered. A conserved physical quantity can help explain a particular continuity, but dharma has no established identity with energy, momentum, or any other conserved scalar.

passages.heading: 4-a-bridge-to-roop-guna-svabhav-and-dharma
passages.section: 4. A bridge to roop, guna, svabhav, and dharma
passages.text: The same care applies to the effort–motion–result account. A physical trajectory provides a succession of configurations and interactions through which the three aspects can be examined together. The source terms bal, shakti, and shram need their defined meanings; translating them as strength, power, and effort does not assign them units of newtons, watts, or joules. Such a numerical correspondence would require a separate operational definition.

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: 5. Niyam, niyantran, and santulan

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: Law, regulation, and balance express connected orderliness. Niyam is the basis for regulating conduct and activity and the way in which activity is preserved and disciplined. Characteristic conduct expresses svabhav and is itself connected with niyam. Niyantran concerns the lawful mutual recognition through which units participate in definite relations; in material units, recognition means constitution-conformant response. Santulan includes the mediative maintenance of balance between generative and dissolutive activities (MVD, pp. 34, 70, 77, 154; SB, pp. 56–57, 62).

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: A unit maintains its definite character and participates in mutual relations. Material conduct is described through result-conformance; pranic regulation through seed-conformance; animal balance through species-conformance. Humans establish conscious order through understanding and sanskar. These characteristic emphases belong to a connected account in which law, regulation, and balance apply across existence (SB, pp. 235–236; MVD, pp. 174–175).

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: The proposed bridge distinguishes three questions within each physical application:

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: Concept Question to make explicit Physical description to investigate Niyam — law What makes the conduct definite under the stated conditions? Evolution equations, admissible states, interaction laws, and their domain of validity. Niyantran — regulation Through what organisation and mutual conditions is that conduct maintained or altered? Constraints, internal couplings, surrounding exchanges, and, where present, feedback that maintains an operating range. Santulan — balance How does the unit’s activity remain coherent with the participating whole? Specified balance relations, bounded operation, persistence, and stability or recovery under stated disturbances, together with effects on other participants.

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: These are complementary analytical questions. A constraint can contribute to law and regulation; a maintained exchange can contribute to regulation and balance. The table does not divide natural orderliness into three independent mechanisms or require a separate controller for every unit.

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: Physical balance also needs a declared meaning. An equality between incoming and outgoing flows, a stationary configuration, and recovery after disturbance answer different questions. Stability analysis can establish a particular form of persistence or return under explicit conditions (LYAP, local stability and LaSalle’s invariance principle). The wider meaning of santulan concerns participation as well as the persistence of a selected subsystem. A device may operate steadily while exhausting the resource that sustains its surroundings. Its steady operation alone would leave the wider question unanswered.

passages.heading: 5-niyam-niyantran-and-santulan
passages.text: For human living, balance requires evaluation of relationships, values, responsibilities, and consequences. Balanced living is connected with justice, and participation in universal orderliness with resolution (MVD, p. 174). The physical description supplies facts that this evaluation must take into account.

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: 6. A worked material example

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: Consider a mass attached to a spring and damper, with an optional external drive. The assembly is a system chosen for analysis; this choice does not by itself classify it as a new compound. Its material components have definite dimensions and constitution. The mass moves, the spring responds to displacement, the damper transfers mechanical energy into heat, and the drive can supply work. Appendix A derives its motion and energy balance.

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: Roop is represented through the assembly’s geometry and its changing configuration. Guna becomes evident in the spring’s restoring response, the damper’s resistance, and the drive’s effect in their actual mutual arrangement. Material svabhav is examined through the maintained organisation and, in an expanded model, its formation or breakdown. Material dharma remains existence: termination of this assembly’s organisation leaves its constituents participating in subsequent material configurations. An ideal spring equation describes only a limited part of that account; it contains no fracture or chemical transformation law.

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: Niyam is expressed through the definite response equations and their assumptions. Niyantran is examined through the attachment constraints, restoring interaction, damping, and specified drive. Santulan is investigated through an explicitly chosen scope: continued motion within the assembly’s operating range, its exchange with the surroundings, and its persistence under disturbances.

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: Three cases expose the distinctions. An ideal undamped assembly continues oscillating after displacement. With damping and no drive, the model approaches its resting configuration. With a periodic drive and positive damping, it can approach a repeating motion in which average supplied power equals average dissipated power. Balance can thus accompany continuing motion and exchange. These statements follow for the specified oscillator; they are not a derivation of universal natural balance (MIT-D, pp. 2–4; Appendix A.3).

passages.heading: 6-a-worked-material-example
passages.text: A resting coordinate also describes only the variable selected by the model. It does not establish that all activity of the material bearer has ceased. This is how a reduced mechanical description can coexist with the ontology’s broader account of continuous unit activity.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: 7.1 Invariant constitution and refinable disposition

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: Jeevan has a constitutionally complete organisation with atma at the centre and buddhi, chitta, vritti, and mun in successive orbits. Its constitution remains complete while its sentient functioning develops. The main study places this fixed organisation in the constitutional description and the changing disposition in a separate persistent profile (MVD, pp. 78, 91; parent study, §§6–7 and Appendix A.3).

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: The extension should preserve that distinction. The variable content concerns understanding, accepted meanings, evaluation references, purposes, sanskar, and the coherence of faculty activity. Faculty existence is invariant. Reports and observations about these states belong in an evidence record; a person’s report of realisation does not, by itself, determine the underlying state.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: This suggests a structured transition account for Jeevan: an encountered situation is recognised through a present understanding; evaluation informs resolve and selection; consequences become available for further examination; study and recognition can revise accepted meanings and dispositions. Such an account may initially use qualitative states and event-based changes. A numerical rate of refinement becomes meaningful only after its variables and observation procedures have been defined.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: 7.2 What can be carried over from mechanics

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: Mechanics offers a disciplined way to separate state, invariant structure, evolution, coupling, and observation. Those distinctions can organise a Jeevan model. The concentric account supplies faculty roles, but it does not supply measured orbital coordinates, conjugate momenta, or a Hamiltonian for semantic change.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: A future variational proposal for Jeevan would therefore need to define the admissible states, their meaningful differences, allowed trajectories, and the functional whose stationarity yields the proposed change. It would then need to show why this construction fits the source account and improves prediction. The first version can proceed with a specified revision relation; a Hamiltonian form is a research question, rather than an entry requirement.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: 7.3 Bodily expression and the interface

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: The body remains a pranic organisation described through its material processes. Its association with Jeevan manifests the human being. The model must connect bodily presentation to sentient recognition and connect resolve and selection to bodily expression while retaining the two units (parent study, §6.4 and Appendix A.3).

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: For a conditional model, observed bodily activity can be supplied as an input to the material model, and reported experience together with observed conduct can inform the proposed refinement model. For a joint prediction, the interface must itself be specified through a functional relation or an empirically estimated rule. Its underlying mechanism can remain unexplained while its input–output behaviour is investigated. Any proposed coupling must remain compatible with the physical equations and exchanges of the chosen system; an assertion of zero added energy alone does not settle that compatibility.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: 7.4 Values, fulfilment, and continuity

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: The knowledge order brings evaluation into conscious participation. Its fulfilment includes happiness, and the highest goal is paramanand with continuity of realisation and fulfilment. Justice concerns recognising and fulfilling relationships through values and their evaluation (MVD, pp. 101, 174, 327; parent study, §§7.8–11; Axiology: Value Theory, §§1.1–1.8).

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: The extension therefore retains the study’s value distinctions: Jeevan values, humane qualities, established and expressed relationship values, and object values. A resource quantity or successful bodily action supplies only part of the evidence. Evaluation must also consider the actual relationship, recognised responsibility, people affected, and continuing consequences. A numerical implementation should use a structured assessment of these requirements before considering any scalar summary.

passages.heading: 7-extending-the-approach-to-jeevan-and-human-participation
passages.section: 7. Extending the approach to Jeevan and human participation
passages.text: Continuity has three connected scopes: continuing realisation in Jeevan, sustained humane conduct through changing situations, and the continuation of understanding and fulfilment through successive participants. A stable behaviour pattern can be examined mathematically, but its stability does not establish its justice or the realisation of paramanand. Families and institutions extend this inquiry through education, shared arrangements, and the transmission of understanding. They remain organisations of participating persons; the extension assigns them no additional Jeevan. Their contribution to akhand samaj, universal human order, and awakened tradition is examined through the continuity of that participation (MVD, pp. 338–339; parent study, Appendix A.11).

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: 8. Development and validation approach

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: The research should advance through bounded applications whose results can be checked independently. The oscillator establishes the mathematical method. A subsequent shared-water example can connect a physical process to evaluation without requiring a complete theory of society.

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: In that example, the material account follows stored water, inflow, withdrawal, and the conditions of delivery. The human account follows needs, actual relationships, agreed responsibilities, reasons for allocation, action, and subsequent evaluation. Water delivered is measurable. Whether the allocation fulfils responsibility requires the relationship and value account as well. If a valve is actuated, its force and energy requirements belong to the physical description; the choice of allocation belongs to the proposed evaluation and interface description.

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: Work package Concrete output Requirement for accepting the result Material specification State dictionary, system boundary, interactions, initial conditions, and adopted equations Reproduce the known example; check dimensions, energy or material accounting, and sensitivity to numerical resolution. Ontological bridge A description of all four aspects and the three orderliness questions for the same example Every correspondence has a clear meaning, scope, and source basis; physical variables retain their scientific definitions. Composite or pranic extension One model of maintained organisation with explicit exchanges Account for the constituents, containing organisation, and changes that invalidate the chosen model. Human participation pilot Separate records for observations, accepted meanings, responsibilities, decisions, and consequences Use observed interface inputs first; state what would be required to predict them. Refinement and continuity Competing revision rules and criteria for continuing fulfilment Compare predictions with later observations; distinguish bodily limitations, circumstances, and changes in understanding.

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: Validation has three distinct tasks. Source review checks the meanings and connections being represented. Mathematical analysis checks whether the proposed equations entail the stated behaviour. Empirical comparison checks whether that behaviour fits observations. Agreement in one task supplies no automatic result in the others.

passages.heading: 8-development-and-validation-approach
passages.text: For the Jeevan pilot, repeated cases must help distinguish competing explanations. The same outward action can arise from different accepted meanings; a person can understand a responsibility while lacking the bodily or material capacity to fulfil it. Observations of reasons, action, consequences, and later revision should therefore be examined together. Finite observations can support evidence of maintained fulfilment over the tested situations; a claim of indefinite continuity needs an additional argument.

passages.heading: 9-issues-requiring-further-work
passages.text: 9. Issues requiring further work

passages.heading: 9-issues-requiring-further-work
passages.text: Issue What remains to be established Physical identification of units Define the scale and map the selected physical system to the ontological description. Specific claims about atomic development and constitutional completeness need their own comparison with contemporary atomic physics. Saturation Clarify whether a physical interpretation is proposed, and what observation could distinguish it. The present equations contain no additional saturation force or energy supply. Boundaries and composition Establish when a changing aggregate counts as a maintained whole and when it dissolves. Match constituent and whole descriptions without counting the same matter or energy twice. Open and pranic dynamics Specify exchanges, reactions, transport, and the operating conditions required for continuing bodily organisation. Meaning of balance Choose the quantities, participants, durations, and disturbances being assessed. Separate local equilibrium, boundedness, recovery, and wider complementary participation. Jeevan’s mutable state Define what a change in understanding, evaluation, or sanskar consists of, and which distinctions can be inferred from evidence. Keep its constitutional architecture invariant. Body–Jeevan coupling Specify both directions of the interface, its timing, and its compatibility with the physical model. Distinguish conditional forecasts from coupled predictions. Variational Jeevan dynamics Justify any proposed state geometry, action functional, or conjugate variables. The existence of a highest value does not select a physical Hamiltonian. Values and measurement Preserve the distinction between material provision, relational fulfilment, and Jeevan’s realisation. Determine which indicators support which claims and where evidence remains incomplete. Refinement and stable fulfilment State the conditions under which correction is retained and conduct remains coherent through new situations. Include conflicting evidence and failures of transfer. Necessity and emergence Preserve the philosophical argument that awakening is the necessary fulfilment of human capacity. A quantitative inevitability claim additionally needs a specified transition law and a proof that its stated conditions ensure the result.

passages.heading: 9-issues-requiring-further-work
passages.text: The last issue is particularly relevant to Hamiltonian language. An unforced canonical Hamiltonian flow preserves phase-space volume. It cannot simply be assigned the attracting behaviour of a dissipative learning process on that same space (Tong-H, §4.2). An account of irreversible refinement needs explicit assumptions about what changes, what is retained, and how interaction or the chosen description makes that change possible. The present note establishes the framework in which those assumptions can be investigated.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: Appendix A. Material dynamics

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: A.1 State, stationary action, and conjugate momentum

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: Let q∈Rd be independent local mechanical coordinates and let L(q,q˙,t) be a smooth Lagrangian. Assume a nonsingular velocity Hessian in the region being considered:

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: Wab=∂2L∂q˙a∂q˙b,det⁡W≠0.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: For fixed endpoint variations, stationary action gives the Euler–Lagrange equations:

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: S[q]=∫t0t1L(q,q˙,t) dt,δS=0,

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: ddt∂L∂q˙a−∂L∂qa=0.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: The local Legendre transformation is

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: pa=∂L∂q˙a,q˙=v(q,p,t),H(q,p,t)=p⋅v−L(q,v,t).

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: It gives

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: An autonomous Hamiltonian is consequently conserved along this unforced flow. Identifying it with physical energy requires the chosen Lagrangian and coordinates to support that identification. Conjugate momentum need not generally equal mass times velocity. Singular Lagrangians and further constraints require additional treatment (Tong-L, §2.1; SICM-H, §3.1; Tong-H, §4.1).

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: A.2 Forcing and dissipation

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: For generalized nonconservative forces Qa not already represented in L,

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: ddt∂L∂q˙a−∂L∂qa=Qa.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: Writing EL=q˙⋅Lq˙−L gives

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: dELdt=Q⋅q˙−∂L∂t.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: In the corresponding momentum coordinates,

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: q˙a=Hpa,p˙a=−Hqa+Qa,H˙=Ht+Q⋅q˙.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: These equations include specified forcing. Their dissipative part is additional to the unforced canonical flow. A Rayleigh function D can represent viscous damping through Qa=Fa−∂D/∂q˙a (MIT-D, pp. 1–3).

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: A.3 Damped, driven oscillator

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: For constant m,k>0, c≥0, and prescribed force u(t), take

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: Then

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: mq¨+cq˙+kq=u(t),p=mq˙,H=p22m+kq22,

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: q˙=pm,p˙=−kq−cmp+u(t),H˙=u(t)q˙−cq˙2.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: For displacement in metres, m is in kilograms, k in newtons per metre, c in newton-seconds per metre, u in newtons, H in joules, and H˙ in watts. D has dimensions of power. These units belong to the mechanical model.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: With u=0 and c=0, nonzero solutions oscillate with conserved energy. With u=0 and c>0, the roots

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: λ±=−c±c2−4mk2m

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: have negative real parts, so all solutions approach the origin. This conclusion follows from the linear dynamics, rather than from energy conservation.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: For u=F0cos⁡ωt, F0>0, c>0, and ω>0, the transient decays and the remaining motion is

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: qss=Acos⁡(ωt−δ),A=F0(k−mω2)2+(cω)2,

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: δ=atan2⁡(cω,k−mω2),⟨uq˙⟩=c⟨q˙2⟩=12cA2ω2.

passages.heading: appendix-a-material-dynamics
passages.text: The brackets denote an average over a full period of the steady motion. Instantaneous energy can vary while the average power balance holds. The calculation instantiates the standard damped-oscillator equations (MIT-D, pp. 2–4).

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: Let X(t) describe the independent physical degrees of freedom selected for the body and surroundings. It gives a quantitative representation of the corresponding parent material states, rather than adding another writable copy. Constituent and whole variables must be linked or derived so that the description does not duplicate physical state. A proposed bounded extension has the form

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: X˙=fphys(X,u,w;θ),y=hphys(X)+ϵ.

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: Here w specifies external conditions, θ the physical parameters, y observed data, and ϵ observation error. The input u is a physical input at a declared boundary. If the actuator is included in X, its dynamics and energy supply are included there as well.

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: For Jeevan j, retain the parent study’s invariant constitution χj and its persistent refinable profile:

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: zj,n=(fj,n,σj,n,kj,n,dj,n,aj,n,qj,n,rj,nacc).

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: These entries concern faculty functioning, sanskar, study and enlightenment, direct recognition, realisation, evaluation references, and the accepted relationship-model. The symbol qj,n here retains the parent’s meaning of evaluation references; it is unrelated to the mechanical coordinates q in Appendix A. No numerical scale is assumed for the profile.

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: An initial update relation can be written

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: zj,n+1∈RJ(zj,n,χj,sj,n,ℓj,n;Δtn),

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: where sj,n is bodily presentation through the interface and ℓj,n is the relevant experienced or studied content, including consequences available for evaluation. Specifying RJ is part of the research. It implements the parent’s single combined disposition-revision event, with its provenance recorded, rather than adding an independent update alongside the parent’s event application. The evidence ledger Ln records reports and observations about these processes and remains distinct from their actual occurrence.

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: The interface retains the parent’s two directions:

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: (uj,b,nB→J,uj,b,nJ→B)∈I(X[tn,tn+1],xj,n,zj,n,ηn,Rη,nactual),

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: where ηn denotes the active body–Jeevan association, xj,n retains Jeevan’s parent state including its invariant constitution, and Rη,nactual retains actual mutuality, including human relationships and roles. Actual relationship is distinct from the accepted relationship-model in zj. The first interface component supplies the presentation represented by sj,n. The second must be connected to bodily expression by an explicit coupling rule; it cannot simply be substituted for a physical force u without such a rule. The material trajectory and interface relation must be solved consistently for a coupled prediction. Observation-based conditional models instead supply the relevant inputs from records.

passages.heading: appendix-b-a-provisional-coupled-description
passages.section: Appendix B. A provisional coupled description
passages.text: This schema instantiates the parent’s separation of constitution, disposition, interface, and evidence (Appendix A.3). It is not yet a closed evolution law: the revision and interface relations, observation procedures, timing, and initial conditions remain to be specified.

passages.heading: glossary
passages.text: Glossary

passages.heading: glossary
passages.text: Term Meaning used in this note Jada The insentient line, including material and pranic units. Jeevan The constitutionally complete sentient unit, distinct from its associated body. Roop / rūpa Form: the unit’s definite configuration and boundary-framework. Guna / guṇa Relative power: operative influence in mutuality. Svabhav / svabhāva Essential nature: the functional character of participation within an order. Dharma Order-specific innateness, with its corresponding meaning of fulfilment. Niyam Law: definite orderliness and conduct. Niyantran Regulation: order maintained through constitution and mutuality. Santulan Balance: coherent maintenance and participation in orderliness. Saturation Units inseparably present within and permeated by satta, retained here as an ontological premise. Mechanical state The physical variables required by a chosen model to describe evolution. Stationary action The variational condition yielding the equations for an adopted Lagrangian. Stability A specified mathematical property concerning behaviour after disturbance. Param anand / paramanand The highest fulfilment, whose continuity concerns realisation and living.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Editorial Notes

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Meaning of the proposed bridge

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The four-aspect meanings are inherited from the primary account and the ontology companion. Their representation through physical variables and the three analytical questions for law, regulation, and balance are proposals of this note. The overlapping source relationships are preserved. No exact identities between roop and coordinates, guna and force, svabhav and a potential, or dharma and a Hamiltonian are asserted.

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: Constitution and physical identification

passages.heading: editorial-notes
passages.text: The source’s nucleus-and-orbit account of Jeevan is retained as the philosophical constitution used by the parent model. This note imports no contemporary particle identification, orbital radius, or mechanical momentum for its faculties. It adopts conventional physics for the material applications it specifies while leaving comparison with the source’s particular atomic-development claims open.
